resale_co.name: Sale Certificate of Occupancy and Certificate of Land Use Compliance
resale_co.issued_by: Building Code Official, Code Enforcement / Building Department (Housing); Land Use Administrator for the Land Use certificate
resale_co.lead_time: The City Code says the Building Code Official inspects within 10 days of the application; the Land Use Administrator acts within 15 days of a completed application. Housing inspections run Monday to Friday, 9:30 am to 1 pm.
resale_co.valid_for: Not stated. A new Certificate of Occupancy is needed whenever the occupants change.
requirements: Curb and sidewalk free of trip hazards (damaged sidewalk or curb must be repaired for the Land Use certificate)
All railings and spindles in place (36 inch rail height)
Window screens in place from May 15 to October 1
ABC fire extinguisher with the gauge in the green, no larger than 10 pounds, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen (required for sales; City pages still list it)
Smoke alarms in each bedroom, on each level and within 10 feet of all bedrooms; CO alarm on each sleeping floor and near any major gas appliance
If smoke detectors are monitored, a certificate from the alarm company
Two outlets in each bedroom; bathroom outlet plus a fan or exhaust window
Water heater pressure relief valve discharge checked
Unit clean: no mold in tub, clean rugs, no chipping paint

resale_co.how_to_apply: Submit two forms from the Housing page to the Building / Code Enforcement Department, City Hall, 6201 Atlantic Avenue: the Sale Certificate of Occupancy Application (buyer, agent, proposed settlement date, whether smoke detectors are monitored, and the adults and children who will live in each unit) and the Application Certificate of Land Use Compliance (seller, property, zoning and use). A Certificate of Occupancy is needed per unit. Pay when the inspection is scheduled (cash, check or card). If the home is sold as is, the buyer becomes responsible for bringing it up to code before the CO is issued.

resale_co.notes: City Code §138-7 (read in full on ecode360) bars selling or transferring any dwelling until the Building Code Official issues a certificate of occupancy, and Chapter 94 requires a certificate of land use compliance before occupancy of any structure. The Code Enforcement FAQ confirms both are needed to sell a home. Fees: the current forms (Sale CO updated 4/11/25; both PDFs dated January 2026) and the City Code fee schedule (Chapter 114, amended 4-10-2025) both give $100 for the certificate of occupancy and $100 for the land use certificate; the FAQ still says $50.00 per form, which looks out of date. If a home is sold as is, the Code makes the new owner responsible for code upgrades before the CO is issued. The Code Enforcement page sidebar lists cmalfara@ventnorcity.org for Housing and dmanera@ventnorcity.org for Building; Pam Learn is listed as Inspector (plearn@ventnorcity.org, 609-823-7987). Rentals need their own CO (monthly and yearly rentals) or a mercantile license (short-term); those are not resale items.

requirements: Smoke alarms: one in each bedroom, one on each level, and one within 10 feet of all bedrooms (battery or hardwired accepted)
Carbon monoxide alarm on each sleeping floor and near any major gas burning appliance, per the manufacturer's instructions

Portable fire extinguisher, required for sales only: ABC type, no larger than 10 pounds, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen, gauge in the green (City letter, 2008 scan, and current FAQ still list it)

authorities.name: Ventnor City Building / Code Enforcement Department (smoke, CO and extinguisher check within the Sale Certificate of Occupancy)
authorities.lead_time: Part of the Sale CO inspection; Housing inspections run Monday to Friday, 9:30 am to 1 pm.
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke certificate application or fee was found. The City's Certificate of Occupancy requirements letter says smoke alarms, CO alarms and portable fire extinguishers are required before any Certificate of Occupancy is issued, and the state fire directory lists the Ventnor City Building Department for smoke detector compliance, so the check is made during the Sale Certificate of Occupancy inspection.

fire_cert.notes: Ventnor's fire code enforcing agency is the Ventnor City Fire Department (LEA code F), but its Fire Prevention and Links and Forms pages list only business, rental property registration and permit forms, with nothing on resale smoke certificates, and the City's Fire Prevention code chapter and fee schedule show no smoke certificate fee. The state fire directory names the 'Ventnor City Bldg Dept' for smoke detector compliance, and the City's CO requirements letter ties the smoke/CO/extinguisher check to the Certificate of Occupancy, so the Building / Code Enforcement Department is listed. Fire Bureau contacts, if needed: the City web page lists Thomas Halpin, Fire Official/Fire Inspector, 609-823-7943, thalpin@ventnorcity.org, and Joseph Iannuzzelli as Fire Inspector (jiannuzzelli@ventnorcity.org); the state directory (survey 5/26/2026) lists Joseph Iannuzzelli as Fire Official. The City letter and FAQ still require a fire extinguisher for sales, although state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped it from the state sale certificate in February 2025.
